stem: A client receives verapamil together with a beta blocker. Which adverse effect is most important for the nurse to monitor?

options.A: Marked tachycardia from additive sympathetic stimulation
options.B: Severe hypernatremia from renal sodium retention
options.C: Excessive bradycardia or atrioventricular conduction block from additive cardiac effects
options.D: Profound hyperglycemia from increased insulin resistance

rationale: Verapamil labeling warns that concomitant beta blockers can produce additive negative effects on heart rate and atrioventricular conduction, including excessive bradycardia and AV block.
educational_objective: Monitor for excessive bradycardia and AV conduction abnormalities when verapamil is combined with a beta blocker.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine
source_locator: Drug Interactions — Beta-Blockers: additive negative effects on heart rate and AV conduction
source_claim_supported: Verapamil plus beta blockers can have additive effects on heart rate and AV conduction, causing excessive bradycardia or AV block.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — cardiovascular drug interactions
correction_summary: Removed overbroad claims about universal heart failure or mandatory avoidance and retained the direct labeled conduction risk.
